standard_prerequisites.name: Completing a morphism on cones
standard_prerequisites.use: Builds the inverse component c' on the cones from the inverse homotopy equivalences a, b, through the left commutative box.

standard_prerequisites.name: The two-out-of-three reduction for triangle morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the assertion to the endomorphism case (1, 1, c) and yields the identity (c - 1)^2 = 0 from the admissible rows of the difference diagram.

core_obligations: Inverting the first two components (proof lines 4271-4286): since a and b are homotopy equivalences they are invertible in K(A); lemma-cone applied to the left commutative box of the inverted diagram supplies a map c' on the cones making the inverted diagram commute.

Reduction to the endomorphism case (proof lines 4287-4296): by lemma-triseq it suffices to prove that for a morphism of triangles (1, 1, c) from a cone triangle to itself, the map c is an isomorphism in K(A).

The inverse of c (proof lines 4297-4319): from the commutative endomorphism diagram, subtracting the identity produces a morphism of triangles (0, c - 1, 0) whose side maps are zero; since the rows are admissible short exact sequences, lemma-triseq gives (c - 1)^2 = 0, whence 2 - c is inverse to c and c is an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Invert a and b in the homotopy category and complete to a morphism of triangles with component c' on the cones.
Reduce by lemma-triseq to the endomorphism case with identity side maps.
Apply the difference trick: (c - 1) squares to zero through the admissible rows, so 2 - c inverts c.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the cone-level two-out-of-three statement for morphisms of cone triangles in the differential graded setting (statement lines 4260-4276). The proof (lines 4278-4319) is a real triangulated-category argument: inverting the first two components through the cone-completion lemma, the reduction to the endomorphism case via the two-out-of-three lemma, and the difference-map trick (c - 1)^2 = 0 from the admissible rows that exhibits 2 - c as the inverse of c. H2: compact, but the reduction logic and the difference trick are genuine content and the statement is a workhorse for the homotopy-category arguments of the chapter.
